## {.smaller}
Term - [validity]{style="font-family:Wingdings"}
: Definition: [the main extent to which a concept, conclusion, or measurement is well-founded and likely corresponds accurately to the real world.]{style="font-family:Wingdings"}. 

Term - [reliability]{style="font-family:Wingdings"}
: Definition: [the overall consistency of a measure. A measure is said to have a high reliability if it produces similar results under consistent conditions]{style="font-family:Wingdings"}. 

Term - [bias]{style="font-family:Wingdings"}
: Definition: [a systematic tendency in which the methods used to gather data and estimate a sample statistic present an inaccurate, skewed or distorted depiction of reality.]{style="font-family:Wingdings"}.

---

validity  
  : the main extent to which a concept, conclusion, or measurement is well-founded and likely corresponds accurately to the real world. 

reliability  
  : the overall consistency of a measure. A measure is said to have a high reliability if it produces similar results under consistent conditions  

bias  
  : a systematic tendency in which the methods used to gather data and estimate a sample statistic present an inaccurate, skewed or distorted depiction of reality.
